sources.title: Leibniz Institute of European History: Baden
sources.note: Direct academic state history: 1771 union, Napoleonic territorial expansion, 1806 grand duchy. Early map polygon is compared against documented later expansion, not endorsed.

sources.title: Karlsruhe City Archives: Religious minorities
sources.note: Indexed original municipal historical article: founding privileges and uneven practical treatment of religious communities.

sources.title: Baden-Württemberg civic education: Constitution of Baden, 1818
sources.note: Direct official modern transcription of primary text, PDF pages 1 to 3: sections 7 to 9, 14, 26 and 37. Exact sample section 14 on page 2; retains Competenz. It is a constitutional promise, not proof of complete practical judicial independence.

sources.title: Stadtwerke Karlsruhe: The beginnings of municipal services
sources.note: Direct municipal utility history: 1759 rapeseed-oil lamps, moonless nights and ruler present; 1764 horse-driven wooden pumping machinery, groundwater three metres deep.

sources.title: TECHNOSEUM: Two wheels, 200 years, school materials
sources.note: Direct museum PDF, printed pages 5 to 6: 12 June 1817 ride about 14 kilometres; wooden construction and plans made by craftsmen; Mannheim bread-roll shrinkage after harvest failure.

sources.title: Karlsruhe literary exhibition: Hebel’s Schatzkästlein
sources.note: Indexed original municipal exhibition entry: 1811 Cotta edition selected 127 pieces from 1808 to 1811 calendars, revised language for wider readership.

sources.title: Karlsruhe City Encyclopedia: Landgraben
sources.note: Direct municipal archive article: systematic sewer expansion from 1883; initial continued cesspit system, cost of water closets and river pollution concerns; 1893 permission for faecal flushing. Explicitly later than imported 1878 cutoff.

sources.title: German Federal Archives: July 1849 at Rastatt
sources.note: Direct/indexed archive chronology: July 7 bombardment, civilian shelter in cellars, palace and fortifications; July 23 surrender, illness among prisoners.

sources.title: Historical Atlas of Baden-Württemberg: Administrative divisions
sources.note: Direct academic atlas PDF, printed page 2: Brauer adapted Code civil; announced 1808 but uniform civil law took effect in 1810.

sources.title: Baden-Württemberg State Archives: Friedrich II’s abdication
sources.note: Direct/indexed archival account and record reference GLAK 230 Nr.154; provisional government November 10, temporary relinquishment November 13, definitive abdication November 22, 1918.

sources.title: Hessian State Archives: Nassau 1866 exhibition
sources.note: Indexed original archive exhibition introduction: duchy 1806 to 1866, territory between Rhine, Main, Lahn and Dill; direct web PDF fetch failed. No reliance on unsupported present-tense dynastic claims.

sources.title: Hessian State Archives: Nassau military administration
sources.note: Direct/indexed archive administrative history, 1806 to 1820: union of Nassau-Usingen and Nassau-Weilburg, agreement of September 5, 1806 and organizational integration.

sources.title: Hessian historical information system: Nassau’s administrative edict
sources.note: Indexed original academic entry via browse/current/141/section/0/pageSize/40/sn/edb: November 1815 administration, 28 districts in 1816, serfdom abolished 1808 and compulsory labor 1812.

sources.title: Hessian historical information system: Nassau school reform, 1817
sources.note: Indexed original academic entry via browse/current/160/section/0/pageSize/50/sn/edb. Compulsory schooling ages six to fourteen, boys and girls, social and religious inclusion; teaching methods and teacher training. Direct old permalink fetch failed.

sources.title: Wiesbaden City Encyclopedia: Hof Geisberg agricultural school
sources.note: Direct official translated article: institute established 1818, moved 1835, winter instruction arranged around farming. German-path fetch failed; uses this directly checked English page. Other secondary accounts differ on 1834/1835 move, so exact move year omitted from prose.

sources.title: Peter Sandner, History of Nassau’s welfare administration
sources.note: Indexed original academic monograph hosted by Landeswohlfahrtsverband Hessen, printed page 42 and note 126: district doctors as public officials, municipalities paid two thirds; 1816 orphan fund, 1820 widows/orphans fund. Later Nazi period is not projected backward; uses only nineteenth-century background.

sources.title: Wiesbaden City Archives: Chronology, 1600 to 1848
sources.note: Direct chronology entries: 1810 Kursaal, gambling location, 1813 to 1820 palace repurposed for museum/library/offices, railway dates March 10 and April 13, 1840.

sources.title: Municipality of Selters: Mineral-water jugs and a shipwreck find
sources.note: Direct municipal reports, Selterswasserkrug in Danziger Bucht: jug around 1820, stamp Selters/HN used 1806 to 1830, one to two million annual jugs; contemporary medicinal reputation not endorsed as medical efficacy. No assertion contents were independently chemically verified.

sources.title: Nassau’s constitutional edict: 1817 printed collection, page 3
sources.note: Direct twice-proofread transcription linked to scan of primary edition: Sammlung der landesherrlichen Edicte, Wiesbaden Hofbuchdruckerei, 1817, page 3. Exact excerpt ends Staats; rendered comma in public prose. Rulers’ self-description, not independent audit of taxation.

sources.title: Wiesbaden City Archives: The demands of the people of Nassau
sources.note: Direct chronology: March 1, 1848 nine demands, leaflets and oral circulation, March 4 acceptance before about 30,000; press/association/religious freedom.

sources.title: Institute for Historical Regional Studies: Himmighofen and Nassau’s end
sources.note: Direct academic regional history: Nassau sided with Austria in 1866, defeat ended independence and Prussia annexed territory. Used for political ending, not to generalize one village’s entire social history.
